evidence: Hor. S. 1.1.121: verbum nōn amplius addam
terms.comment: “Nothing further” is nihil amplius; “further” things, as in further news, are plūra.

evidence: Liv. praef. 4: rēs est praetereā et immēnsī operis
Tac. Germ. 2.2: quis porrō … Germāniam peteret
Quint. 12.11.6: quid porrō est honestius quam docēre quod optimē sciās?
terms.comment: First of all “onward, further on” (see “forward”); hence, in an argument, “and further”.

terms.grammar: with the indicative; also accēdit ut with the subjunctive

evidence: Caes. BC 3.57: ut praeter auctōritātem vīrēs quoque ad coercendum habēret
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “of that besides which there is something else in addition, besides, together with, in addition to”. It also means “except”: hoc nēminī praeter mē vidētur (Cic. Att. 1.1.2, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: jam satis est. … verbum nōn amplius addam
phrases.english: that’s enough now. I won’t add a word further

phrases.latin: auctius atque dī melius fēcēre. bene est. nīl amplius ōrō
phrases.english: the gods have done more, and better, than I asked. It is well. I ask nothing further

phrases.latin: rēs est praetereā et immēnsī operis
phrases.english: besides, the task is one of enormous labour
